identity.headquarters: San Francisco Bay Area (Palo Alto), USA

value_chain.value_chain_position: Vertically integrated model creator spanning training infrastructure, foundation models, and consumer/enterprise distribution. xAI trains Grok models on its own Colossus supercomputer (555,000 NVIDIA H100 GPUs, 2 GW capacity) in Memphis, TN, giving it rare self-sufficiency in compute. Upstream, xAI depends on NVIDIA for GPUs and Supermicro for server assembly. Downstream, it distributes Grok through the X platform (primary consumer channel for 600M+ monthly active users), a developer API (docs.x.ai), and enterprise subscriptions (Grok Business/Enterprise). The Feb 2026 SpaceX acquisition ($250B for xAI in a $1.25T combined entity) further integrates xAI into the Musk ecosystem spanning connectivity (Starlink), energy (Tesla Megapack), and vehicles (Tesla).

key_products: Grok 4 / Grok 4.1 (Nov 2025): frontier reasoning models. Grok 4 offers 256K context at $3/$15 per M tokens (input/output), competitive with GPT-5 and Claude Opus on major benchmarks. Grok 4.1 features a 2M token context window (tied for industry-leading with Gemini 3 Pro), 3x lower hallucination rate than Grok 4, and drastically lower pricing at $0.20/$0.50 per M tokens. Grok 4.1 Fast is optimized for speed with Agent Tools API for autonomous agent workflows.

Grok chatbot (integrated into X): AI assistant available to X users with real-time internet search, image generation (Aurora), and multimodal reasoning. Free tier with limited access, SuperGrok at $30/month, SuperGrok Heavy at ~$300/month. Used by millions of X platform users daily.

Grok API platform: developer API at docs.x.ai offering Grok 4, Grok 4.1, and Grok 4.1 Fast models. Supports text, vision, and function calling. EU endpoint (eu-west-1) available for data residency. Prompt caching offers 50-75% discounts. Free credits up to $175/month for developers. Agent Tools API enables fully autonomous agent capabilities.

business.business_model: Multi-stream: (1) Consumer subscriptions via SuperGrok ($30/mo) and SuperGrok Heavy (~$300/mo); (2) Enterprise subscriptions via Grok Business and Grok Enterprise (launched Dec 2025); (3) Usage-based API pricing ranging from $0.20/M tokens (Grok 4.1 Fast) to $3/$15 per M tokens (Grok 4); (4) Government/defense contracts (DoD ceiling ~$200M-$300M); (5) Integration revenue via X platform (Grok embedded for X Premium subscribers). Targeting profitability by 2027.
business.burn_rate_and_runway: Approximately $1B/month burn rate, driven primarily by massive GPU infrastructure buildout ($18B+ in GPU purchases) and operational costs for the 555,000-GPU Colossus cluster. Following SpaceX acquisition (Feb 2026) and $20B Series E, runway is effectively unlimited through SpaceX's balance sheet (SpaceX generated ~$15B revenue, $8B profit in 2025) and planned IPO.

openness.open_vs_closed_spectrum: Hybrid. Grok-1 (314B MoE) was open-sourced under Apache 2.0 (Mar 2024, weights only). Grok 2.5 released as open-weight under Grok 2 Community License Agreement (Aug 2025), which allows free use and modification but prohibits use for training other AI models. Grok 3 expected to go open-weight in early 2026. Frontier models (Grok 4, Grok 4.1) remain proprietary and API-only. Overall trajectory: older models gradually open-sourced, current frontier models kept closed.

startup_relevance.relevance_for_startups: xAI/Grok matters for entrepreneurs in several distinct ways: (1) Price-competitive API: Grok 4.1 at $0.20/M input tokens is among the cheapest frontier-class APIs, with up to $175/month in free credits, making it an affordable alternative to OpenAI/Anthropic for startups; (2) 2M context window: Grok 4.1's industry-leading context enables use cases (long document analysis, code repository understanding, legal review) that shorter-context models cannot address; (3) Real-time data advantage: Grok's deep integration with X/Twitter provides unique access to real-time social media data unavailable to other LLMs, valuable for startups in social listening, news analysis, trend detection, and brand monitoring; (4) Agent-native API: the Agent Tools API (server-side tools for autonomous agent workflows) positions Grok as a first-class platform for AI agent startups, an emerging category; (5) EU data residency: eu-west-1 endpoint with GDPR/CCPA compliance and SOC 2 Type 2 certification makes Grok viable for European startups in regulated sectors; (6) Musk ecosystem distribution: integration across X (600M+ MAU), Tesla vehicles, and potentially Starlink creates unique distribution channels that startups building on Grok can leverage; (7) Open-weight models: Grok-1 (Apache 2.0) and Grok 2.5 (restrictive license) offer self-hosting options, though the anti-training restriction on Grok 2.5 limits fine-tuning compared to DeepSeek or Llama; (8) Platform risk: xAI's trajectory is tightly coupled to Elon Musk's broader business and political activities -- startups should factor in reputational and regulatory risks associated with the Musk ecosystem.
startup_relevance.accessibility: Highly accessible for developers. Grok API offers competitive per-token pricing starting at $0.20/M input tokens (Grok 4.1 Fast), with up to $175/month in free credits. EU endpoint (eu-west-1) available. Consumer access through X platform (free tier with limited Grok access, SuperGrok at $30/month). Enterprise plans available (Grok Business, Grok Enterprise) with GDPR/CCPA compliance and SOC 2 Type 2 certification. No dedicated startup credit program identified. Open-weight Grok-1 (Apache 2.0) and Grok 2.5 (restrictive license) available for self-hosting on Hugging Face. API documentation at docs.x.ai.
startup_relevance.primary_model_dependency: Self-sufficient. xAI develops Grok models internally using Colossus infrastructure (555,000 NVIDIA H100 GPUs). Depends on NVIDIA for GPU hardware.

ecosystem.key_partnerships: NVIDIA: $2B strategic investment in Series E, primary GPU supplier for Colossus. SpaceX: acquired xAI in Feb 2026 ($1.25T combined entity), plans for orbital data centers powered by Starship launches. Tesla: $2B investment in xAI, supplies Megapack batteries for Colossus power, Grok integrated into Tesla vehicles. X (formerly Twitter): xAI acquired X Corp in Mar 2025 ($33B all-stock), X serves as primary distribution channel (600M+ MAU) and real-time data source for training. Supermicro: server assembly partner for Colossus. Cisco: strategic investor in Series E. Key financial investors: a16z, Sequoia, BlackRock, Fidelity, QIA, MGX.
ecosystem.competitive_moat: Unmatched compute scale: Colossus (555K GPUs, 2 GW) is the world's largest AI supercomputer, with plans for 1M+ GPUs, giving xAI a training capacity advantage only matched by Google and Microsoft. Unique real-time data: X platform integration provides live social media data unavailable to competitors, enabling differentiated training data and real-time information retrieval. Musk vertical integration: Tesla (energy, vehicles, robotics), SpaceX (connectivity, orbital compute), and X (distribution, data) create a cross-company moat spanning hardware, energy, data, distribution, and applications -- no other AI lab has this level of ecosystem integration. Speed of execution: 100K GPU cluster built in 122 days (record pace). Capital access: $42B+ raised in under 2 years, SpaceX acquisition providing access to even larger capital through planned IPO.
ecosystem.data_moat_type: Proprietary training data / User feedback loop / Distribution

regulatory.regulatory_exposure: GPAI provider under EU AI Act for Grok models (frontier models likely exceed 10^25 FLOPs systemic risk threshold). xAI signed the EU GPAI Code of Practice (Jul 2025) but only committed to the 'Safety and Security' chapter, opting out of transparency and copyright clauses -- must demonstrate compliance via alternative means. EU investigation expanded (Jan 2026) into Grok following deepfake/non-consensual intimate imagery crisis, with potential penalties up to 35M EUR or 7% of global turnover under AI Act Article 5. Full deepfake labeling requirements under AI Act take effect Aug 2026. Grok Business/Enterprise offer GDPR and CCPA compliance with SOC 2 Type 2 certification and EU endpoint. The SpaceX merger and Musk's political activities (DOGE involvement) create heightened EU scrutiny. DoD contracts indicate significant US government entanglement that may complicate EU sovereignty requirements.
